archetype.name: Pocket Passer (distributor)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who wins from a mostly clean pocket by spreading the ball across four or five targets, and this year is pushing it farther downfield than he has in years.

report.headline: Goff is throwing deeper and cleaner, and a broken defense keeps him throwing
report.take:
Goff is who he has been in Detroit: a pocket thrower who needs protection, gets it, and turns it into efficient volume. Through four games he sits 8th in EPA per dropback (0.289) and 7th in adjusted net yards per dropback. That is almost exactly his 2024 level (0.293 EPA/play, 5th), not a new player. He has been pressured on only 16.1% of dropbacks, 7th-lowest, and when pressure does come he goes down at about his usual rate. His 25.9% pressure-to-sack sits right next to 2024's 25.4% and 2025's 25.3%. That is who he is, so it is not a new flaw.

What has changed is how far he throws. His aggressiveness is 18.0% after five straight seasons between 10.7% and 12.9%, and his intended air yards are 8.17 after back-to-back 6.8 aDOT years. The payoff has been large. On 41 intermediate throws he is at 0.793 EPA, and on 11 deep attempts he is at 1.359. Those passes are carrying the efficiency line. The short game (0.162) is solid, and the screen game behind the line (-0.232) is a drag. He is also spreading the value around. Amon-Ra St. Brown gets the most targets (46) but the lowest return of the top five (0.176 EPA/target). LaPorta (0.583), TeSlaa (0.511) and Jameson Williams (0.496) are doing the damage downfield.

The context explains the volume. Detroit's defense ranks 32nd in EPA and dead last against deep passes. Every Lions game has gone over the total, and Goff has thrown 64 passes while trailing by nine or more, at 0.418 EPA. Many of those were catch-up throws against defenses protecting a lead. The 412-yard, 52-attempt game at Carolina was a loss. Volume is inflated by the defense, and the yards will keep coming as long as it stays this bad.

Some numbers will move the wrong way. He has zero interceptions on 161 attempts after posting 7 to 16 in every full season of his career. He also has three turnover-worthy fumbles and none lost. Third down has been poor: -0.105 EPA, 35.9% conversions, and a -12.1 CPOE facing an average 7.6 yards to go. The interior line is thin, with guard Ben Bartch out and center Cade Mays on IR until around Week 7. Expect the efficiency to settle somewhere between his 2024 and 2025 levels, with the yardage staying high.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep efficiency
strengths.body: His 10-19 and 20+ yard throws have produced huge EPA, and he is attempting them more often than he has in years. The rise in aggressiveness looks like a deliberate shift in play design, with LaPorta, Williams and TeSlaa working downfield. The deep sample is only 11 throws, so the size of the edge will shrink. The more aggressive profile looks real.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, consistent processing
strengths.body: He is among the least-pressured passers in the league. When kept clean he is reliably efficient: his 0.289 EPA per dropback matches his best season. This depends on the line more than on him, which matters with two interior starters hurt.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: Eight of his nine touchdowns came on 34 red-zone attempts, at a positive 4.1 CPOE. He has always been a high-TD passer in this offense, with 30 or more TDs in each of the last three seasons. The rate is a bit hot, but the role is stable.

concerns.title: Zero turnovers won't hold
concerns.body: No interceptions on 161 attempts is the best rate among qualifiers. His career says 8-12 picks a year is normal for him. He also has three turnover-worthy fumbles without losing one. The new downfield aggressiveness adds interception risk, so expect the clean sheet to end soon.

concerns.title: Third down has been poor
concerns.body: On third down he is converting barely a third of the time with a deeply negative CPOE, and three of his eight sacks came there. Long average distances (7.6 to go) explain part of it. A -12.1 CPOE also points to missed throws. Over four games this is partly noise, but it is the clearest gap in an otherwise efficient line.

concerns.title: Thinning interior line
concerns.body: Guard Ben Bartch (93% of snaps) is out and center Cade Mays is on IR, targeting Week 7. Goff's season rests on a clean pocket. His pressure-to-sack rate is mid-pack, so added interior pressure would turn into sacks and rushed third downs rather than scramble value. His five scrambles have produced zero first downs.

trend.note: After a modest opener (5.9 pass EPA, 206 yards against New Orleans), he has topped 12 pass EPA in three straight games. Yardage has climbed with the shootouts, peaking at 412 at Carolina, though that day produced only one touchdown.

nextGame.headline: Arizona's leaky pass defense and stout run front funnel volume to Goff
nextGame.body:
Arizona has a split defensive profile that suits Goff. The Cardinals rank 5th against the run but 31st in pass EPA. They are also 31st in explosive passes allowed, 30th on deep throws and 31st on short throws. Detroit's own run game is only 17th in EPA, so the easiest path is through the air, and the Cardinals give up 2.75 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks (30th). Their pass rush is middling: 23rd in hit rate, 12th in sack rate. That matters more than usual given Detroit's line injuries.

On Detroit's side, Bartch is out and Mays is still weeks away, so the interior protection is the soft spot to watch. For Arizona, safety Andrew Wingard (76% of snaps) is questionable with a knee bruise. If he sits, a secondary that already leaks explosives gets thinner, which helps Goff's newfound downfield game. Arizona also lost left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. for the season. That weakens a Cardinals offense already 23rd in pass EPA, so this may not become the track meet Detroit's defense usually invites.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield passing vs. explosive-prone secondary
keyMatchups.body: Goff's intermediate and deep throws are where his value comes from, and Arizona is among the worst in the league at preventing big pass plays. That is the strongest overlap on the board.

keyMatchups.title: Run game hits a wall
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's run defense is a top-five unit, and Detroit's rushing offense is middling. Expect Campbell to lean on the pass and on Gibbs as a receiver, which pushes up Goff's attempt count.

keyMatchups.title: Patched interior vs. average pass rush
keyMatchups.body: With Bartch out, Arizona's ordinary hit rate is the main threat to the clean pocket Goff relies on. If the backup guard holds up, Goff's usual baseline is in play. If not, his third-down issues get worse.

nextGame.watch: Whether Wingard plays for Arizona, and how often Goff is hit with Bartch out. That decides whether the deep game gets going or the night turns into checkdowns and third-down sacks.

restOfSeason.body:
Detroit's defense guarantees him volume. As long as it ranks last in EPA and last against deep passes, Goff will throw 38-42 times a game and pile up yardage regardless of efficiency. His efficiency should come down from 0.289 toward the 0.20-0.25 range: the deep-ball rate on 11 attempts is unsustainable, and the third-down struggles cut the other way, so the net is a modest decline rather than a collapse. Interceptions will arrive at something like his career rate, roughly one every 50-60 attempts, especially with the more aggressive throw profile.

The TD rate should stay healthy because the red-zone role is stable. Mays' return around Week 7 should help a pocket that is currently patched together. The downfield shift is the real question. If it holds, he can match his 2024 output. If he drifts back to his usual 12% aggressiveness, expect efficiency closer to 2025.
swingFactors: Whether Detroit's last-ranked defense improves and reduces shootout volume
Health of the interior line (Bartch, Mays)
Whether the higher downfield aggressiveness sticks

bets.reason: Arizona is 31st in pass EPA but 5th against the run, and Detroit's run game is 17th, so volume should tilt to the air. He has averaged just over 40 attempts a game. The risk is that his average is inflated by the 412-yard game.
Arizona allows 2.75 passing TDs a game to QBs (30th), and Goff has thrown 8 TDs on 34 red-zone attempts. His role near the goal line is steady.

Detroit is 0-3-1 against the spread and lost outright at Carolina as a 4.5-point road favorite. A defense ranked 32nd in EPA makes laying points on the road hard to trust, even against a Cardinals offense missing its left tackle.

All four Detroit games have gone over, averaging about 58.5 combined points, and Arizona's pass defense is nearly as porous as Detroit's. The caution is Arizona's 23rd-ranked passing offense, now without Paris Johnson Jr.

confidence.note: Four-game sample with an outlier deep split, but efficiency matches his 2024 baseline and the matchup is clear.
